thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High error rate detected for /v1/generate (hosted) — KV cache memory rising rapidly on tp-shard clusters in us-west-2. NCCL stall patterns observed. paging triggered.

incident-bot: metrics snapshot: 99th latency spike +400ms, kv_cache.mem_used +82% in 3m, nccl_retries increased x6. Affected model: redwood-3b-quant-tp.

maria: @kevin i'm paged — jumping in now. Where are we seeing the mem blowups?

kevin: seeing it on tp-shard group tp-45* (4xA100). KV cache growth per-shard is uneven: shard-2 and shard-3 showing repeated cache re-allocs/evictions and then memory cliff. NCCL logs show timeouts between devices 1<->2.

eli: pushing logs from the runtime:
```
[2026-03-15T18:05:12Z] kv_shard 2: cache_growth=+1.9GB/s, evict_rate=0.0/s
[2026-03-15T18:05:14Z] nccl: retry(3) timeout wait 2000ms on peer 1
[2026-03-15T18:05:16Z] tp_shard: uneven_partition detected, expected=0x3f, got=0x2f
```

maria: rough customer impact? any 5xx?

ops-bot: Incident severity: P1. 1200 requests failed in last 5m. Top customers: alpha-fin (latency alarms), beta-chat (observed truncation). Automated fallback to non-sharded kv not active for this model (not enabled).

sam: ping from CS — alpha-fin is already calling. they're seeing timeouts in production chat flows. Need ETA for mitigation.

kevin: immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce continuous batching window to 10ms for tp-45*, 2) disable KV shard rebalancing on that cluster, 3) roll a runtime hotfix that forces uniform shard assignment (fallback to mod-based mapping), 4) if that fails, fail open to disabled-KV-cache for that model and fall back to local tmp cache.

maria: i'm going to run the config changes for batching first (lowest risk). applying to tp-45a now.

kevin: i'll prepare the runtime hotpatch PR (small change to shard mapping):
```
// force deterministic mod mapping during recovery
if (runtime_mode == RESTRICTED_RECOVERY) {
  shard_id = token_hash % num_shards;
}
```

eli: heads-up: that change disables some of the dynamic balancing heuristics. acceptable short-term. needs canary on a single host first.

maria: batching change applied to tp-45a/b/c/d. confirm reduced window and batch_size cap=8.

ops-bot: Config deploy log: apply-config tp-45*: continuous_batch_ms=10, max_batch_size=8 — success on 4/4 hosts.

kevin: monitoring...

eli: nccl stalls frequency dropping on tp-45a/b — peer timeouts reduced. kv cache growth slowed but still skewed on shard-2.

maria: good. rolling the runtime hotpatch canary to tp-45a (single card process). kevin do you want me to create a canary label?

kevin: yes label=kv-shard-fix-canary. canary deploy started.

ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime-hotfix/kv-shard-map v1.0.1 -> tp-45a.

eli: canary logs show re-mapping stabilized token->shard distribution. memory delta normalized across shards on tp-45a within 90s.

maria: canary looks good. rolling to tp-45b and tp-45c, leaving d for now as rollback target. doing staged 2/3.

sam: alpha-fin reports reduced timeouts after ~4m. still occasional 503s but much better.

ops-bot: Request fail count trend: 5m failures down from 1200 -> 230. 99th latency down 400ms -> +50ms.

kevin: after roll to b/c we still see small eviction bursts on shard-2. hypothesis: residual unflushed prefix caches from previous imbalance. suggesting graceful cache purge across shards during low traffic window.

maria: scheduling rolling cache purge for tp-45d in 10m. coordination: set autoscale to no-scale to avoid flapping during purge.

eli: purge command: 
```
./kvctl purge --cluster tp-45d --shard shard-2 --mode=steady --throttle=150MB/s
```

kevin: also pin routing policy to prefer non-sharded variant for high-QPS customers until purge completes (alpha-fin routing override).

sam: applied alpha-fin override to non-sharded route at 18:16 PST. alerting them and explaining mitigation steps.

maria: purge started on tp-45d shard-2. throughput throttle in effect.

ops-bot: NCCL retries returned to baseline. Cache mem usage normalized across shards after purge.

eli: performing post-mortem data capture. capturing kv_cache histograms, nccl logs, batch profiles. saving to s3://redwood-incident-archives/1824509123/

kevin: root cause (working theory) — a recent continuous batching tweak (auto-batch horizon increase) combined with an edge-case in TP partitioning logic allowed uneven token->shard assignment on shard rotation, leading to hot-shard growth followed by NCCL stalls when peers awaited missing KV pages. The auto-batching increased in-flight KV refs so memory blowups amplified quickly.

maria: immediate action items: 
- revert auto-batch horizon change in next release (eli)
- add safety cap to per-shard cache growth metric with automated throttle (kevin)
- enable non-sharded fallback for models with tp_shard config unset (platform)
- add canary for shard rebalancer changes (maria)

eli: longer term: smarter shard balance checks, stronger invariant tests for token->shard mapping, and simulation harness for continuous-batching + TP combos.

sam: CS follow-up: prepare customer impact summary for alpha-fin and beta-chat and runbooks for support to provide status updates.

maria: handing off to next oncall @kevin at 18:24 PST. summary pinned: batching window reduced, runtime canary rolled to tp-45b/c, cache purge completed on d, alpha-fin routed to non-sharded temporarily. ongoing: monitor for 2h.

kevin: ack takeover. will monitor metrics and start implementing safety cap. tagging this for postmortem.

ops-bot: Handoff: incident owner changed from maria -> kevin at 1824509067. (pager log entry)

maria: thanks all. will post a short postmortem draft after we have artifact captures.

kevin: adding a note — we should also check Dedicated clusters that run similar models; create ticket INF-4923 to sweep.

ops-bot: Incident resolved->monitoring. Final metrics: failures down to baseline within 35m.

maria: closing pager; will reopen if regressions seen.

sam: filed customer notes and sent escalation emails to alpha-fin ops.

eli: uploading logs and artifacts now. link: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-incident-archives/1824509123/manifest.json

incident-bot: [CLOSE] Incident marked resolved by kevin.
